items.stem: In alphabetical filing, which name is filed FIRST?  Felipe R. Cruz | Dr. Victoria T. Dela Cruz | Mario P. Lim | Engr. Elena G. Navarro

reveal.terms: "Indexing" means writing a name in filing order: surname first, then given name, then middle initial. A title such as Dr. is the last unit.
reveal.shortcut: Rewrite each surname as one block: drop spaces and hyphens, keep the prefix (Dela Cruz = DELACRUZ). Then compare letter by letter (ARMA Rule 1). Order: Felipe R. Cruz → CRUZ, Felipe; Dr. Victoria T. Dela Cruz → DELACRUZ, Victoria; Mario P. Lim → LIM, Mario; Engr. Elena G. Navarro → NAVARRO, Elena.
reveal.why_correct: "Felipe R. Cruz" is right. It comes first when every name is indexed surname first, letter by letter. This follows the standard office filing rule (ARMA International Simplified Filing Standard Rules, Rule 6), not a rule published by the CSC. Source standard: ANSI/ARMA 12-2005.

why_wrong.o1: "Engr. Elena G. Navarro" sorts by the given name. Personal names file by surname first.
why_wrong.o2: "Mario P. Lim" files as LIM, which comes after CRUZ.
why_wrong.o3: "Dr. Victoria T. Dela Cruz" sorts by the title (Dr., Atty., Engr.). A title is only the last unit.
